note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), bundled as library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz and read offline (owb-am). Every Scripture quotation was re-quoted to it verbatim (founder decision, 2026-11-18: Amharic quotes OWB everywhere), replacing the 1962/2003 UBS wording and the translator-rendered Old Testament verses the first edition carried.

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: the whole verse, the shortest contiguous span carrying the quoted clause, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…'. Epigraphs Murray sets one line per paragraph are re-cut line by line to OWB's clauses and order (Ps 33:20-22, Ps 130:5-6, Isa 40:27-31). Unmarked recitations are quotations too.

Murray's refrain 'My soul, wait thou only upon God!' is OWB Ps 62:5, «ነፍሴ ሆይ፣ በእግዚአብሔር ፊት ብቻ ጸጥ በዪ!» (short form «በእግዚአብሔር ፊት ብቻ ጸጥ በዪ»), identical in every chapter (requote decision `wait-only-upon-god`). OWB reads 'be silent', the margin Murray himself cites on Day 1; the introduction bridges it once, and the author's own 'waiting' in prose stays መጠበቅ. Other recurring verses keep one OWB span throughout: Isa 30:18 «እርሱን የሚጠባበቁ ሁሉ በእውነት የተባረኩ ናቸው», Ps 25:5 «ቀኑን ሙሉ የምጠብቀው አንተን ነው», Ps 37:34 «በእግዚአብሔር ተስፋ አድርግ፤ በመንገዱም ጽና», Lam 3:25, Ps 27:14, Isa 40:31.

Where OWB drops the word Murray argues from, one sentence of his prose bridges it once rather than rewriting his teaching: Ps 33:18 'the eye of the Lord' (Day 10), Ps 37:7 'patiently' (Day 11), Ps 40:3 'in my mouth' (Day 14), Ps 46:10 'be still' (Day 26), Isa 27:3 'every moment' (Day 31, per the `every-moment` decision).

`self_rendered` rows (each with a why) are allusions and the author's restatements; the prayers that turn Ps 25:3 into a petition ('Let none that wait on Thee be ashamed', OWB's words with ይድናሉ → ይዳኑ, Day 6); and the A.V. reading of Isa 64:4 on Day 23, which Murray sets against the R.V. — OWB reads with the R.V., which is quoted verbatim there.
